definitions.explanation: One of the ten standard cloud genera: a flat, featureless, low-altitude cloud sheet that covers large areas of sky, often producing drizzle or mist. Distinguished from cumulus by its uniform layered appearance.

examples.japanese: {山|やま}に{層雲|そううん}がかかっている。
examples.english: Stratus clouds are hanging over the mountain.

examples.japanese: {朝|あさ}、{低|ひく}い{層雲|そううん}が{町|まち}を{覆|おお}っていた。
examples.english: In the morning, low stratus clouds covered the town.

examples.japanese: {層雲|そううん}は{霧雨|きりさめ}を{降|ふ}らせることがある。
{層雲|そううん}は{最|もっと}も{低|ひく}い{高度|こうど}にできる{雲|くも}で、{地表|ちひょう}に{接|せっ}すると{霧|きり}と{呼|よ}ばれる。
examples.english: Stratus is the lowest-altitude cloud type, and when it touches the ground it is called fog.

notes:
Composed of {層|そう} (layer) and {雲|うん} (cloud). One of the ten standard cloud classifications ({十|じゅう}{種|しゅ}{雲形|うんけい}) used in meteorology.

USAGE:
- A meteorological term used in weather reports, textbooks, and sometimes in everyday descriptions of overcast conditions.
- Used as a plain noun; does not take する.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {低|ひく}い{層雲|そううん}: low stratus
- {層雲|そううん}がかかる: stratus hangs (over an area)
- {層雲|そううん}が{広|ひろ}がる: stratus clouds spread out

RELATED WORDS:
- {積雲|せきうん}: cumulus — puffy, vertically developed clouds
- {高層雲|こうそううん}: altostratus — stratus clouds at middle altitude
- {乱層雲|らんそううん}: nimbostratus — thick stratus producing steady rain
- {霧|きり}: fog — ground-level stratus
